function: Near-field wideband XL-MIMO channel estimation from pilots received through random ±1 selection matrices, using an implicit deep unfolding network with infinite depth (pp. 1-3).
system: Uplink OFDM near-field XL-MIMO: BS with 256 antennas, 4 RF chains, single-antenna users, 16 subcarriers, 16 time slots, 5 paths, 100 GHz; no RIS (pp. 2, 4).
method: INN-DUNet: deep unfolding with a residual CNN prior sub-network and a gradient-step sub-network, solved as an implicit fixed point (depth-infinity); supervised MSE training with Adam (pp. 2-4).
data_channel: Own simulated near-field spherical-wave channels (eq. 2) with 5 paths, distances U(10,30), angles U(-π/2, π/2); 12000/2000/2000 training/validation/test samples; no standard model (p. 4).
test_conditions: Default 5 paths and 2000 held-out test samples, SNR -4 to 6 dB (Fig. 3); mismatched test with 3 and 7 paths (Fig. 4b) (p. 4).
baselines: Learned: DUNet [8] with 15 and 20 layers (earlier paper of the same group). Non-learned: LMMSE, polar-domain OMP, polar-domain SOMP [3], BPD-OMP [5] (p. 4).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR (Fig. 3), validation MSE per epoch (Fig. 4a), NMSE for 3, 5, 7 paths (Fig. 4b), FLOPs and online time (Table I) (p. 4).
complexity: Table I (p. 4): INN-DUNet 1.16 GFLOPs vs DUNet 2.27 G (15 layers) and 3.02 G (20 layers); online time 6.5025 s, versus 1.6830 s for LMMSE.
q1_support: p. 4: "We generate all dataset based" on the own near-field spherical-wave model of eqs. (2)-(5), with distances U(10, 30) and angles U(-pi/2, pi/2); no 3GPP model, public dataset or measurement is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 4: "under mismatched channel conditions" the NMSE is not significantly affected for different numbers of paths (Fig. 4b, L = 3, 5, 7, against the default L = 5); the paper does not spell out the training value of L for Fig. 4b.
q3_support: p. 4: "the DUNet [8] mentioned in Section II" is an earlier learned estimator of the same group, while LMMSE, P-OMP, P-SOMP [3] and BPD-OMP [5] are non-learned; all are compared with INN-DUNet on NMSE versus SNR in Fig. 3.
q4_support: p. 4: "Table I shows the computational complexity of different methods" by FLOPs and online time: INN-DUNet 1.16 G FLOPs against 2.27 G and 3.02 G for DUNet with 15 and 20 layers, online time 6.5025 s.
q5_support: p. 4: "We generate all dataset based" on the own model (5), with 12000, 2000 and 2000 samples for training, validation and testing; no code or data link, no public dataset and no availability statement appear on pp. 1-5.
notes: Included in area 2: deep unfolding with trained parameters is learned (Step 1.3); near-field XL-MIMO channel estimation, no RIS. q2 rests on the phrase mismatched channel conditions and the L = 3, 5, 7 legend of Fig. 4b; the paper does not state the training L for that figure, so the reviewer should confirm. q3 counts DUNet [8], an earlier paper with overlapping authors, as the learned baseline; INN-DUNet extends it with implicit depth, so a reviewer could see it as a variant. Table I gives FLOPs only for the learned methods (p. 4).
